subject: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity pricing & GPU/throughput sizing for FigLeaf
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Asha Ramanathan <asha@figleaf.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: dedicated capacity sizing, throughput & target $/1M tokens

Hi Asha — thanks again for a productive call earlier. Quick recap and the asks we agreed to: 

1) High-level target & constraints
- Target workload: user-facing summarization + reranking for customer support (batch+sync mix).
- Peak concurrency target: ~180 concurrent sessions; average session ~1.2k tokens output.
- Monthly token baseline: 250M tokens/month, with a 3x burst scenario up to ~750M tokens/month during seasonal peak.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 600ms for short prompts (<= 512 tokens)

2) Throughput / reserved sizing we discussed
- Desired throughput target: sustained 350k tokens/min (~5.8k tokens/sec) typical, peak ~1.7M tokens/min.
- Preliminary recommended lanes: 4–6 GPU lanes depending on GPU type and quantization.

3) GPU options (tradeoffs we highlighted)
- A100 80GB (float/amp): good fit for high-token throughput with established latency predictability.
- H100 80GB (suitable when you prioritize raw throughput for longer contexts; better for 16-bit kernels)
- 4-bit quantized variants (Triton/compiled paths) can materially reduce per-token cost but need evals on quality/regression.

4) Unit economics / budget guidance (initial targets)
- Your target $/1M tokens: you mentioned wanting something in the ~$75–$150/1M tokens range depending on SLA and retention.
- For planning: conservative pricing (no commitment) maps to ~$180–$220/1M tokens for an H100-backed single-lane config; reserved 12+ month commitments with 3–6 lane reservation can get into the $65–$120/1M tokens band depending on quantization and batching.

5) Action items / next steps
- Asha: confirm typical tokens per request distribution & percent of long-context calls (>=2k tokens) so we can finalize lane sizing.
- FigLeaf procurement: share procurement cadence / PO timeline so we align contract/discount cadence.
- Redwood: we will produce a small-slab pricing worksheet with 3 reference configs (A100 x4, H100 x4, H100 x6) + expected $/1M tokens and latency estimates.
- Proposed follow-up: technical sizing call w/ infra team next Wed 5/26.

Attachments: FigLeaf_Redesign_SOW_v1.pdf (attached) — placeholder SOW you shared in the call.

If any of the numbers above are off, flag them and I’ll update. Otherwise we’ll aim to get the pricing worksheet and a draft SOW for signature next week.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

---

From: Asha Ramanathan <asha@figleaf.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@figleaf.ai
Date: 2027-05-22T16:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: dedicated capacity sizing, throughput & target $/1M tokens

Thanks Vanessa — appreciate the summary and the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side so you size appropriately: 

- Tokens per session: median 1.1k, mean ~1.6k (heavy tail due to some diagnostic exports). About 18% of calls exceed 2k tokens.
- Expected ramp: 250M in month 1 of pilot, 500M by month 6, 1.2B by month 12 if pilot converts.
- Budget band: Procurement is budgeting $85–$140/1M tokens for committed capacity, with flexibility for incremental discounts if we commit 12 months+ and provide forecasting.
- Procurement timeline: We need commercial terms and a draft SOW by 6/3 to get approval at our 6/10 procurement committee.

Also attaching our internal SLA priorities (short doc) — please assume compliance and audit evidence will be required. For the technical call, can you include an estimation for a 10M tokens/day steady-state baseline (what lanes and GPU type we should choose for that profile)?

Regards,
Asha
Head of Product
FigLeaf Inc.

On Fri, May 22, 2027 at 2:10 PM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com> wrote:
> (original message attached)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Asha Ramanathan <asha@figleaf.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-23T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: dedicated capacity sizing, throughput & target $/1M tokens

Asha — thanks for the clarifications. I ran a quick config math and attached a compact pricing worksheet (dedicated_pricing_sheet.xlsx) — key points inline below: 

1) Quick config for 10M tokens/day (~116 tokens/sec sustained)
- Recommended: 1 H100 lane (80GB) with optimized batching + prefix cache for your distribution.
- Expected p95 latency: ~450–550ms (depends on prompt length mix).
- Rough unit econ (no commitment): $~195/1M tokens.
- Rough unit econ (12m reserved, 4-lane pool shared): $~95/1M tokens.

2) For the 250M/month baseline (sustained ~96k tokens/min)
- A 3-lane H100 reserved pool with 4-bit quantization trials looks like the lowest-cost path to hit your $85–$140/1M target; 4–6 lanes if you want headroom for 1.2B/12m growth.

3) Discount mechanics & commit bands
- 6-month reserved: ~12–18% off list vs on-demand
- 12-month reserved: ~25–40% off list (depends on lanes & model quantization)
- Additional multi-year or enterprise SLAs can increase discount 2–8% depending on volume guarantees.

4) Risks / blockers to confirm
- If >20% of calls are long-context (>=4k tokens) we should consider additional memory-optimized lanes or a hybrid approach.
- Quantization trials can reduce cost materially but require eval to ensure output quality for ranked summaries.

Next steps from Redwood side (concrete):
- I’ll schedule the infra sizing call for Wed 5/26 10:30am PT (inv to follow)
- Ben / Marissa: please review the attached pricing sheet and confirm availability of H100 capacity for a June pilot. If H100 is constrained, fallback A100 numbers are in the sheet.
- I’ll prepare a draft SOW & initial commercial term sheet for review by 6/1 so FigLeaf can start procurement review.

Link to HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/figleaf-rdw-023
DocuSign intent: I will send pricing + SOW for signature once we align on lane count and commit term.

Best,
Vanessa

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>

Subject: INTERNAL: FigLeaf — next steps & owners (pricing + capacity check)

Ben / Marissa — quick internal summary + who owns what: 

- Ben: please validate H100 availability for a 4-lane reserved pilot starting 6/7 (duration: 30 days) and surface any constraints from capacity planning. If H100 limited, produce A100 fallback numbers by EOD 5/25.
- Marissa: please finalize the dedicated_pricing_sheet.xlsx with the three reference configs (A100 x3, H100 x3, H100 x4) and include the per-1M token estimates we discussed (on-demand vs 12m commit). Attach the sheet to the HubSpot deal and flag the two discount bands for procurement.
- Me (Vanessa): I’ll draft the SOW and a commercial term summary and aim to have them in DocuSign for Asha by 6/1. Also will run a brief quantization-quality risk note with Applied ML to include in the SOW appendix.

Goal: have pricing + SOW ready for FigLeaf procurement review by 6/3. If we can accelerate the infra call earlier, we should.

Thanks — V
